Pressure washing Fort Worth properties, old and new

Fort Worth is the second-largest city in the metroplex, with 918,915 residents in the 2020 census, and it spreads across five counties: Tarrant, Denton, Johnson, Parker and Wise. That reach means pressure washing here covers everything from older brick homes in historic districts like Fairmount to newer subdivisions on the city's edges, plus a lot of commercial frontage.

Dallas Power Washing Pro does not send anyone out. It is a free phone line. Call, say what you need cleaned in Fort Worth and how big it is, and an automated assistant transfers you to an independent, locally owned pressure washing company. That company quotes and does the work, and you pay it directly.

Fort Worth requires a permit for mobile power washers

Most North Texas cities regulate wash water. Fort Worth also regulates the washer. The city requires a permit for "any person or business who engages in mobile commercial cosmetic cleaning," which is the city's term for mobile pressure and power washing.

The permit

$25 for the business and $25 to register each wash unit. One year, not transferable. Vehicles and trailers must be registered, with numbers displayed on each side.

The water

No wash water off the property or into the storm drain, manholes strictly off limits, and any discharge passed through an oil absorbent boom or pad.

The penalty

Up to $2,000 per occurrence for permit or discharge violations, and illicit discharges are a criminal offense, the city says.

For a homeowner or business, that gives you an easy question to ask any company working in Fort Worth: "Can I see your city permit?"

Four Fort Worth things to raise when you call

1

Historic brick and stone

The city lists thirteen neighborhood historic districts, among them Fairmount, Mistletoe Heights, Elizabeth Boulevard, Morningside and Historic Carver Heights, plus the innermost Stockyards district. Older brick and mortar need the gentlest method there is.

2

Watering days

Fort Worth's year-round schedule allows no sprinkler watering on Mondays and bans sprinklers from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with hand-held hoses allowed any time. In a declared drought, ask the water department before washing.

3

Hail country

A 2012 CBS Texas report, citing National Weather Service records and the Insurance Council of Texas, put Tarrant County first in the state, with about 800 hailstorms since 1955. After a big storm, get the roof looked at before anyone cleans it.

4

Commercial frontage

Sundance Square, the Stockyards and miles of retail corridors mean a lot of storefront, patio and drive-thru cleaning, all of it under the city's permit and discharge rules.

Wash water in Fort Worth: the plain version

The city's FAQ for commercial cleaners says it has been illegal to discharge any type of wastewater off-property in Fort Worth since the turn of the century. It points washers to the sanitary sewer through a clean-out stub, sink or suitable indoor drain, or to a grit trap on site, and warns that most outdoor floor drains lead to the storm sewer. It also warns never to open a manhole, and notes that excessive dirt in storm water can break the state's standard for suspended solids.

In practice, a good company covers the curb inlet, controls where rinse water runs on your lot, and recovers it when it has used cleaners. If a company shrugs at the question, keep looking.

Common questions

Who does pressure washing in Fort Worth?

Independent local companies. This line does not wash anything. It answers your call any hour and transfers you to an independent, locally owned pressure washing company that serves Fort Worth, which inspects, quotes, does the work and is paid by you directly.

Does a pressure washing company need a permit in Fort Worth?

For mobile commercial cleaning, yes. Fort Worth requires a permit for any person or business engaged in mobile commercial cosmetic cleaning: $25 for the business, plus $25 to register each wash unit, good for one year. Ask a company for its permit before it starts.

Can wash water go into the street drain in Fort Worth?

No. The city says wash water must not leave the property or enter the storm drain, and that it bans the pollutants washed off a surface, not just the cleaning chemicals. Discharges must pass through an oil absorbent boom or pad, and fines can reach $2,000 per occurrence.

Can I have my house washed on any day in Fort Worth?

Fort Worth's year-round watering schedule limits irrigation systems and sprinklers to set days and bans them from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., while hand-held hoses may be used any time. The page does not address pressure washing, so if a drought stage is declared, check with Fort Worth Water Conservation before booking.

Do I need approval to pressure wash a house in a Fort Worth historic district?

Washing is usually maintenance, but Fort Worth's historic districts, such as Fairmount, Elizabeth Boulevard and Mistletoe Heights, come under the city's historic preservation program, which reviews exterior changes. Gentle cleaning is the safe choice. If you plan to paint, strip or alter masonry, check with the city's preservation staff first.
